topic: Secondary Growth: Cambium, Annual Rings and Bark
title: How Does a Tree Get Thicker? Explained Simply | PUC Biology Class 11
description:
Aarav counts the rings on a fallen tree in the park, light and dark, one inside the other. How does a stem get thicker every year, and why are the rings two colours?

You will see primary growth (length) next to secondary growth (girth), then a zoom ladder from a tree trunk to its cross-section and the cambium zone, with secondary xylem inside and secondary phloem outside. The cambial ring forms step by step in a young dicot stem (intrafascicular and interfascicular cambium), the trunk grows ring by ring through spring wood and autumn wood, and we compare heartwood with sapwood. Then the cork cambium builds the periderm (phellem, phellogen, phelloderm), we see what bark really contains, a pause and think check, a worked example naming three zones of a log, the exam trap about bark, an original NEET pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself. Note: secondary growth is not in the current rationalised NCERT text but is in the ISC (CISCE) Class 11 syllabus.

This is Episode 55 of our PUC Biology series.

Made for NCERT, CBSE, ISC (CISCE), PUC (Karnataka) and NEET students.
